responses.summary: Adversarial review (2 rounds): attribution partially sound; initial accounting gap (351 vs 432) resolved in follow-up after conv1 exclusion explained (ingestion incomplete, ~10 records); remaining weaknesses: selection bias (exclusions should follow predefined criteria), unverified diagnoses (need logs + clean reruns), judge validity (same model answerer/judge), end-to-end reliability. Most important weakness: missing pre-/post-fix counterfactual on identical questions — 49/67 above 50% shows threshold attainment, not causal effect of the fix.

Attribution plausible but not logically established: dirty-run failures explain aggregate collapse, but healthy-subset uplift may reflect difficulty/composition differences rather than the fix. Caveats: post-hoc exclusion risk, data integrity needs log/artifact verification, denominator consistency, comparability across runs, prespecified-threshold interpretation, fix isolation needs controlled before/after run. Baseline comparison (2-question 0% vs 67-question subset) not statistically defensible as improvement evidence — descriptive only. Verdict: dirty-data explanation credible; efficacy claim stronger than evidence supports; clean reproducible full rerun or paired evaluation needed.
